resources.string: Tap Going to bed when you turn in, and I\'m up when you get up. Those two taps define your night.
This night started on %1$s, %2$s ago. Did you forget to tap I\'m up?
The microphone is hearing complete silence. Check that microphone access isn\'t switched off in quick settings, and that no other app is using the mic.
SleepTight needs the microphone to measure how loud your room is. It only keeps sound levels, never audio. Your taps still record the night either way.
The microphone couldn\'t be used. Another app may be using it, such as a call or a voice recorder.
Android stopped SleepTight in the background. Allow it to run without battery restrictions so this doesn\'t happen overnight.
Notifications are off, so there\'s no tracking notification. Tracking still works.
Android can stop apps in the background while you sleep. Let SleepTight run without battery restrictions so it keeps measuring until you get up.

On Samsung phones, also open the app\'s settings, then Battery, and choose Unrestricted. Make sure SleepTight isn\'t listed under Sleeping apps or Deep sleeping apps (Settings → Battery → Background usage limits).
Shown while SleepTight is measuring sound levels overnight
Tells you if overnight tracking stopped
Measuring sound levels only. No audio is recorded.
SleepTight stopped measuring sound levels. Open the app to resume.
Wakes you gently between %1$s and %2$s, as soon as you start to stir
No snoozes left. Time to get up.
Your alarm volume is off, so the alarm will only vibrate. Turn up the alarm volume in your phone\'s sound settings.
SleepTight isn\'t allowed to set exact alarms, so the alarm can\'t ring on time. Allow \"Alarms & reminders\" for SleepTight.
SleepTight can\'t show the alarm over your lock screen. It will still ring, but you\'ll need to unlock to stop it. Allow full-screen notifications for SleepTight.
Notifications are off, so the alarm can\'t show its screen or Snooze and Dismiss buttons. It will ring for up to 10 minutes; open SleepTight to stop it.
A nudge 30 minutes before your bedtime goal
Time to start winding down. Your goal is to be in bed by %1$s.
That time hasn\'t happened yet. Pick an earlier wake time.
Your phone\'s clock is earlier than your bed tap, so the night can\'t be closed. Check the date and time settings.
Listening runs all night, so keep the charger connected.
On the nightstand, next to you
Within arm\'s reach, not under the pillow.
The mic is in the bottom edge: turn that end towards your pillow.
Press and hold, so a bump in the night can\'t end it
The sleep score arrives once there\'s sleep data (Garmin import or the activity estimate).
No nights in this range yet. Tap Going to bed tonight.
Stages appear here once Garmin data is imported, or as an estimate from the night\'s activity.
Tap a sound to hear it at your alarm volume. On the night, it starts quietly and rises over a minute.

A summary of the night from 0 to 100, made of five parts: duration, efficiency, deep and REM sleep, interruptions and regularity. Each part shows its points and what was measured. The dial\'s arc is the score: a full circle is 100.
How long you were asleep compared with your sleep goal of %1$s. The full %2$d points at or above your goal, and proportionally fewer below it.

The share of your time in bed that you were actually asleep. 0 points at %1$d\u00A0%% or less, rising to the full %2$d points at %3$d\u00A0%% or more. Healthy adults usually manage %4$d\u00A0%% or more.

The share of your sleep spent in deep and REM sleep, the stages that matter most for physical recovery and memory. 0 points at %1$d\u00A0%% or less, rising to the full %2$d points at %3$d\u00A0%% or more. It needs sleep stages from Garmin; without them, these points are shared out across the other parts.

Starts at %1$d points. Each wake-up (awake for %2$d minutes or more after falling asleep, not counting the last one before you get up) costs %3$d, and each cluster of noise events (events within %4$d minutes of each other) costs %5$d. Never below 0.

How well you kept your goals that night, each scored from 0 to 1: in bed by %1$s, asleep for %2$s, at most %3$d snoozes, and a steady bedtime over the last %4$d nights. The average of the four, times %5$d.
